title: The Legend of Betsy Ross
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with banter about recent West Coast live shows (Seattle, Portland, San Francisco) and the Brooklyn show, then examine the Betsy Ross legend. They cover Ross's real life as a Quaker-raised upholsterer born Elizabeth Griscom in 1752, her three marriages (John Ross, Joseph Ashburn, John Claypool), and her expulsion from the Quakers after eloping. They then describe the flag story popularized by her grandson William Canby's 1870s speech, the Charles Weisberger painting, and why historians doubt it: no documentary evidence, Washington's implausible presence, and Congress not adopting flag details until June 14, 1777. They discuss Francis Hopkinson's claim for designing the flag, early colonial flags (Pine Tree, Gadsden, Sons of Liberty, Grand Union), reasons the myth spread (national mythology before the centennial), flag symbolism, and close with listener mail about Atari and the E.T. and Superman cartridges.

segments.title: Opening banter and West Coast tour recap
segments.summary: Hosts thank fans for the Seattle, Portland, and San Francisco shows and the movie Crushing It live event, discuss a presentation glitch, a Busy Phillips interview, and plans for more live shows.

segments.title: Introduction to Betsy Ross and the Weisberger painting
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Betsy Ross as a real person and describe the painting The Birth of Our Nation's Flag by Charles Weisberger, whose inscription credits Ross with making the first national standard.
topics: Birth of Our Nation's Flag painting

segments.title: Betsy Ross's early life and Quaker upbringing
segments.summary: Elizabeth Griscom, born in 1752 in Pennsylvania to Samuel and Rebecca, is raised as a strict Quaker among nine surviving children. Her great-grandfather Andrew Griscom was an early Philadelphia carpenter. The hosts describe Quaker beliefs and customs.

segments.title: Upholstery career and marriage to John Ross
segments.summary: Ross apprenticed at about fifteen to upholsterer John Webster and is described as an upholsterer rather than a seamstress. She met and eloped with Anglican John Ross, who came from a well-connected family and was related to George Ross, and was expelled by the Quakers.

segments.title: Widowhood, Free Quakers, and later marriages
segments.summary: John Ross died during the Revolutionary War, possibly from militia service or illness. Ross rejoined the Quakers through the Free Quakers, then married Joseph Ashburn, who died in a British prison, and later John Claypool, with whom she had five daughters. She died in 1836.

segments.title: The Betsy Ross flag legend
segments.summary: The hosts recount the legend: Washington, George Ross, and Robert Morris visit her shop in June 1776, she suggests changing the star to five points, and the flag is adopted. The story came from grandson William Canby's 1870s speech based on family lore.

segments.title: Historians' doubts and Francis Hopkinson's claim
segments.summary: Historians find no documentary evidence for the story: Washington was not in Congress, Congress did not detail a flag until 1777, and a disputed 1851 painting is cited. Francis Hopkinson's claim for payment for a naval flag is discussed as the more documented design credit.

segments.title: Early colonial flags and why the myth spread
segments.summary: The hosts describe early colonial flags including the Pine Tree, Gadsden, and Sons of Liberty flags and the Grand Union flag. They explain the myth's appeal as national mythology before the centennial and its inspirational value for women.

segments.title: Flag symbolism and vexillology
segments.summary: The hosts describe the thirteen stripes and stars, the meanings of red, white, and blue, the study of flags called vexillology, and the Star Spangled Banner at the Smithsonian.

segments.title: Listener mail about Atari
segments.summary: A listener who worked at Atari recounts the Superman cartridge burial and the E.T. cartridge story, and the hosts thank him.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and email contact information and sign off.
